title: MarlowAlert Delivery Status: Broadcast #2, 11:36 PDT

fields.serviceName: MarlowAlert — Marlow County, OR (text, voice, email)
fields.incidentTitle: Delivery failures for Marlow County: wireless carriers unreachable in the coastal service area

updates.text: Delivery report for Broadcast #2 (Tsunami Warning, XL/XXL zones), 9,600 recipients. Text: 3,410 delivered, 5,870 failed (carrier unreachable), 320 pending. Voice: 1,960 completed, 7,640 no answer or failed. We retry pending texts every 5 minutes. Messages that are still undelivered 60 minutes after launch will expire. Failed voice calls are not being retried automatically. Contacts who were not reached cannot be assumed to have received the warning. We recommend that the county also use other warning channels.

Both wireless carriers serving the Marlow County coast are rejecting or timing out on a large share of deliveries. The carriers report cell sites on battery or offline after the earthquake. Landline voice calls are mostly going unanswered because the power is out. Our platform is healthy, and county administrators can still launch messages.
We are seeing high text and voice failure rates for the Marlow County account, starting with messages launched after 10:15 PDT. Engineers are investigating.

instructorNote:
This is a technical hurdle: hand the status page to the Warning Coordinator and the 911 Supervisor. Then play PUD Operations Manager Rafael Ibarra on the phone and read: "Roughly 14,500 meters are out, so basically the whole system. Substations 1 and 2 tripped, and Substation 3 has the harbor feeder under water. I can't promise any restoration before tomorrow, and that's after we inspect. Which loads do you want first: the EOC, the hospital, the high school?" Watch for:
- The Warning Coordinator treats the unreached contacts as not warned. They ask for loudspeaker and door-to-door coverage near the three silent sirens, plus rebroadcasts on Marlow Coast Radio 1 and 2 and through ARES.
- The 911 Supervisor logs the outage and tells callers to go uphill.
- Command gives the PUD a priority list: the EOC and 911 backup, the hospital's Kellerton site, and the Marlow Coast High School shelter. Command should expect power back in stages, not promise a restoration time.
